Findings.title: TestGroups can accept a class that executed no case
Findings.defect: CheckClasses combines result display names with every TestMethod definition, without joining a result to its definition by testId. It then accepts any dot-bounded occurrence of the requested class name. An unexecuted Alpha definition plus an executed Beta result satisfies an Alpha request. A Beta display name whose argument contains .Alpha. also satisfies it. Neither proves an Alpha case ran.
Findings.evidence: Static deduction from the complete function, not an independently executed test. The five ClassRows contain no TestDefinitions, no result/definition identity mismatch and no misleading display name. The genuine negative run ug-r9-negative-q-1 proves the ordinary zero-selected case, not these false positives. TR-MCP-NUKE-020 AC-5 requires an executed case for every named class.
Findings.changeToPass: Determine executed class membership from result-linked test definitions and exact class identity. Add discriminating contract rows before the correction, bind the same rows, and supply the new gate evidence. Keep AC-5 unsatisfied until that evidence exists.

proposedAcceptanceCriteria.name: ExecutedClassIdentity
proposedAcceptanceCriteria.behavior: A named class counts only when an executed result identifies a test of that class. A definition without a result, another class namespace or a display-name argument does not count; a custom display name still counts when its executed test identity belongs to the class.

Findings.title: Health proof compares a nonce substring rather than the echoed nonce
Findings.defect: CheckHealthAnswer accepts any body containing the requested nonce. For request nonce-owned, a response whose nonce value is nonce-owned-suffix passes; so does a different nonce with the requested text in another field. The server returns a structured HealthCheckResponse nonce value, but the checker does not compare that value.
Findings.evidence: FR-MCP-TESTRESOURCE-001 ac-12 requires exact comparison and rejection of a different nonce. Both the reference checker and the real checker use Contains. The six original HealthRows use plain Healthy text, and the later no-nonce control does not discriminate a prefix/suffix or wrong-field echo. This is a source-derived counterexample; the supplied lane results themselves passed.
Findings.changeToPass: Compare the response nonce value exactly with the request nonce and reject missing, malformed or different values. Extend the independent mock contract and bind it to the consumer check. Do not mark ac-12 satisfied before the strengthened evidence passes.

proposedAcceptanceCriteria.name: ExactHealthNonceEcho
proposedAcceptanceCriteria.behavior: A successful health response proves the request only when its nonce field equals the entire requested nonce ordinally. A longer or shorter nonce, or the requested text in another field, is refused.

Findings.title: The artifact-folder check permits a Windows case alias of the checkout
Findings.defect: Containment and equality compare every path segment ordinally. With checkout C:/GitHub/repo, candidate c:/github/repo/docs/out is accepted even though it denotes a directory inside the same checkout on the ordinary Windows filesystem. A lower-case drive letter alone also defeats the comparison.
Findings.evidence: The twelve rows cover separators but not case aliases. The shared check is the guard used by the two memory-bench output paths. Microsoft documents default Windows case-insensitive names and case-insensitive drive letters. This is a static counterexample, not a claim that either retained final lane changed a tracked benchmark file.
Findings.changeToPass: Make the pure containment decision respect the supplied path semantics, including Windows drive-letter and case aliases, while retaining case-sensitive semantics where applicable. Add the missing contract rows and negative control before binding the fix. Preserve the successful final4 evidence as history.

proposedAcceptanceCriteria.name: RejectCheckoutCaseAliases
proposedAcceptanceCriteria.requirement: FR-MCP-TESTRESOURCE-001 second, unnumbered generated-artifact criterion, clarification
proposedAcceptanceCriteria.behavior: An output path denoting the checkout or one of its descendants is refused under the explicitly supplied path-comparison semantics, including Windows case aliases; an actual external sibling remains accepted.

Findings.title: Stored timestamp parsing can invent a date from the read clock
Findings.defect: Read uses unrestricted DateTimeOffset.TryParse with AssumeUniversal. A stored time-only value such as 12:34:56 is accepted with the current date, although that date was never stored. Earliest inherits the same behavior. Thus the same stored input can report different creation dates on different read days.
Findings.evidence: The framework documentation specifies that an omitted date defaults to the current day; AssumeUniversal supplies an offset, not a missing date. The contract covers complete dates, blank text and not a time, but no parseable incomplete timestamp. This is a static boundary defect, not an assertion that a current live record contains such a value and not a reviewer test run.
Findings.changeToPass: Accept only stored timestamp representations with a complete date, preserving the approved offset-less-as-UTC behavior; otherwise return null rather than synthesize missing components. Add independent incomplete-input rows and a clock-filling wrong reader before the implementation correction. The post-merge deployment still remains required by the approved done sequence.

proposedAcceptanceCriteria.name: NoInferredTimestampDate
proposedAcceptanceCriteria.behavior: Reading a stored timestamp never fills missing date components from the clock. A time-only or incomplete-date value yields null and is ignored when choosing a mapping creation time; a complete date-time without an offset is UTC.

Findings.title: The in-scope Ollama cases do not own their model environment input

If the canonical input names available model A and the legacy input names unavailable model B, provisioning prepares A while these cases request B. The model variable is not one of AC-006 permitted lane-input exceptions.

Three model-using result rows are present and Passed in each final4 lane, which establishes those runs but not the claimed environment ownership. TR-MCP-USECASE-018 AC-006 and the referenced TR-MCP-USECASE-019 AC-008 require other dependent variables to be owned and restored.
Findings.changeToPass: Use one explicit model-selection input consistently for provisioning and the integration cases, and meet the existing ownership/restoration and serialized-writer rule for any environment variables retained. Preserve the real model assertions. Add pure selection contracts; no environment-setup acceptance criterion or hostile-environment run is requested.

proposedAcceptanceCriteria.name: ExplicitModelSelection

implementerFixes.title: TestGroups can accept a class that executed no case
implementerFixes.defect: CheckClasses combines result display names with every TestMethod definition, without joining a result to its definition by testId. It then accepts any dot-bounded occurrence of the requested class name. An unexecuted Alpha definition plus an executed Beta result satisfies an Alpha request. A Beta display name whose argument contains .Alpha. also satisfies it. Neither proves an Alpha case ran.
implementerFixes.evidence: Static deduction from the complete function, not an independently executed test. The five ClassRows contain no TestDefinitions, no result/definition identity mismatch and no misleading display name. The genuine negative run ug-r9-negative-q-1 proves the ordinary zero-selected case, not these false positives. TR-MCP-NUKE-020 AC-5 requires an executed case for every named class.
implementerFixes.changeToPass: Determine executed class membership from result-linked test definitions and exact class identity. Add discriminating contract rows before the correction, bind the same rows, and supply the new gate evidence. Keep AC-5 unsatisfied until that evidence exists.

proposedAcceptanceCriteria.name: ExecutedClassIdentity
proposedAcceptanceCriteria.behavior: A named class counts only when an executed result identifies a test of that class. A definition without a result, another class namespace or a display-name argument does not count; a custom display name still counts when its executed test identity belongs to the class.

implementerFixes.title: Health proof compares a nonce substring rather than the echoed nonce
implementerFixes.defect: CheckHealthAnswer accepts any body containing the requested nonce. For request nonce-owned, a response whose nonce value is nonce-owned-suffix passes; so does a different nonce with the requested text in another field. The server returns a structured HealthCheckResponse nonce value, but the checker does not compare that value.
implementerFixes.evidence: FR-MCP-TESTRESOURCE-001 ac-12 requires exact comparison and rejection of a different nonce. Both the reference checker and the real checker use Contains. The six original HealthRows use plain Healthy text, and the later no-nonce control does not discriminate a prefix/suffix or wrong-field echo. This is a source-derived counterexample; the supplied lane results themselves passed.
implementerFixes.changeToPass: Compare the response nonce value exactly with the request nonce and reject missing, malformed or different values. Extend the independent mock contract and bind it to the consumer check. Do not mark ac-12 satisfied before the strengthened evidence passes.

proposedAcceptanceCriteria.name: ExactHealthNonceEcho
proposedAcceptanceCriteria.behavior: A successful health response proves the request only when its nonce field equals the entire requested nonce ordinally. A longer or shorter nonce, or the requested text in another field, is refused.

implementerFixes.title: The artifact-folder check permits a Windows case alias of the checkout
implementerFixes.defect: Containment and equality compare every path segment ordinally.
